items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: When we was with Desdun, I think the first, when we left, we were going on that tour

ctx.x: Yeah, otherwise there were a tough bunch of them.

Yeah, it was a tough bunch of them. It was pretty much. The first job that, I think it was about the first job I never got paid on, I played at the corner club. I don't mean the club, the club paid them the job, but this fella by the name of Munson Hickman, he had a job and we was all youngsters, you know, and he got the money in front. See, and he went and take another job, he sent us on that job so we go to collect our money because we played the dance, the man said, well we paid Hickman off already. So we…

items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1963-03-29
items.q: we was playing with Desdun, we was playing the advertisement

ctx.x: Well, I think we're about to run out a little bit now.

Well, let's not leave George McCollum out, Alvin Alcorn. See, as you talk, you think, you see? Think like George McCollum. George McCollum was a, he ain't number one trumpet man, but he was better when you put the music up there too. He was great. I remember one time in Basin, Mississippi, we was playing with Desdun, we was playing the advertisement. George McCollum picked up a number, nobody knew what number and what it was, but it sounds some good. And everybody fell right on in there with him, and the people…

items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: when Desden was making up the band, we- Pierron No. 2.

ctx.x: Were you in the band then, Harold, when that happened?

Yeah. When Tymy came in the band, when Desden was making up the band, we- Pierron No. 2. Yeah. We had, that's when the oil force said, Felice Goff, Shine, Ram and Brown Trombone, Old Man Kimball Bass. What's Shine?
Is that Shine played with Sam? Nolan Williams. Nolan Williams. Yeah, Shine. Made the record with Sam Wilson.
